plants.norway-maple: dense, broad, rounded dome on a short stem, scalloped outline; shade core visible in the gaps at 1:200 to 1:50, leaf and samara marks at 1:50; reads as a Norway maple at every scale.
plants.field-maple: small rounded dense crown on a short stem, 10 m; clearly the small brother of the other two maples.
plants.sycamore-maple: large broad dome, 25 m, heavier and wider than the Norway maple; 1:500 one calm outline.
plants.horse-chestnut: massive dense dome, 24 m, large overlapping sprays; the candles are small dots at this size; reads as a horse chestnut.
plants.european-beech: wide dense dome on a smooth stem; the top is ragged at 1:200 and 1:100 (separate sprays and bare shoots at the tip), the 1:500 top now joins the crown.
plants.common-ash: open, airy, oval crown of separate sprays with the limbs showing, which fits the species; at 1:500 one round spray stands on the tip like a knob.
plants.japanese-cherry: vase of steep limbs under a flat-topped cloud of blossom clusters; the best reading asset of the scope.
plants.saucer-magnolia: low, wide, multi-stemmed, goblets as small circles on the masses; reads as a magnolia in bloom.
plants.crab-apple: low dense dome on a short forked stem with a drooping skirt; small rectangular opening in the upper crown at 1:500 and 1:200.
plants.ginkgo: irregular narrow cone of separate clusters on ascending limbs, fan marks at 1:50; reads as a young street ginkgo.
plants.honey-locust: open vase of long limbs with flat sprays; thin, and one cluster stands alone on a long bare leader above the crown.
plants.sweetgum: regular pyramid of clusters on a straight stem; star marks at 1:50.
plants.tulip-tree: tall, narrow, straight stem to a third of the height, foliage clouds over a darker core.
plants.red-oak: broad, heavy, rounded crown on a short stout stem with spreading limbs.
plants.black-locust: open, irregular crown with separate foliage clouds and bare forks, as the species has.
plants.rowan: small oval crown on a slender stem, berry clusters as dots at 1:200 to 1:50; bubbly close up.
plants.hawthorn: low, broad, flat-topped dense small tree; the plan has an open ring around the centre.
plants.black-alder: narrow cone on a straight stem; the 1:500 reads as stacked tiers.
plants.norway-spruce: narrow cone of drooping tiers with upturned ends, sun and shade halves toned; unmistakable.
plants.european-larch: thin, widely spaced storeys with the stem showing between them and hanging shoots at 1:50 and 1:100.
plants.atlas-cedar: flat needle plates in tiers on ascending limbs with sky between; unmistakable.
plants.italian-cypress: slender dark column of overlapping upright sprays; unmistakable at every scale.
plants.english-yew: broad dark dome of a few large masses on a short, thick, fluted trunk.
plants.dawn-redwood: narrow pyramid on a flared base, but as separate beads on a stick.
plants.olive-tree: short, massive, gnarled stem with a broad low crown wider than high; reads as an old olive.
plants.fig-tree: broad, low, multi-stemmed dome in tiers; reads as a small multi-stem tree, not specifically as a fig; top tier detached at 1:200.
plants.stone-pine: tall bare stem under a flat umbrella of needle plates; unmistakable.
